doc.title: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan Jaffe, Sandra Jaffe Interview, 1961-11-25
doc.interviewee: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan Jaffe, Sandra Jaffe

title: How the hall found its musicians
summary: Allan Jaffe describes the earlier informal sessions in the landlord's gallery, Russell's and Grayson Mills's help, and getting George Lewis to play.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, really, when we started, there was a group of people involved in this person we rent from now, Larry Bornstein, had been running these sessions on an informal basis. That would be, I guess, for at least 10 years. The band would come in occasionally during the night when they weren't playing. He'd open up his gallery to them and pass the kitty and pay them in from that. Mr. Russell had been down here for quite a while doing research on the musicians. And a boy here from California by the name of Grayson Mills who did a lot of initial work in getting the musicians started. Once the men started playing and a lot of other men started finding a way around to us, still there are a lot of people we would like to get to play for us that haven't been around. The only way we really know about the men are still around are through people like Mr. Russell and people who do come around.
How did you get hold of these men in the first place? Did they find out about you?
Well, these men are, you know, live here. Yeah. And a lot of them are quite famous. People like Jim Robinson, George Lewis, Kit Howard, I mean...
Excuse me for interrupting you here, Alan, but you said George Lewis. Now Lewis has just returned from Europe. How do you get him to come back here and play a one-night or a two-night stand?

George is happy to. George likes to play. He likes to be heard. He's happy to play with any band who he can work with. And I mean by working with, I mean, this is people who he can produce the type of music with that he wants to.
